title: fix(nodes): stop interrupted camera and location reads during lookup
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Ctrl+C leaving camera and location reads waiting for node lookup to respond or time out, including the legacy paired-node lookup.

## User Impact

Interrupted reads close their lookup connection and exit 130 without starting a node operation. Lookup uses the existing command cancellation owner; already-dispatched mutation RPCs retain their response custody.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared node resolver now forwards the command's existing signal to both lookup methods. This closes the preparation gap without adding state, a lifecycle owner, or caller-specific cancellation plumbing.

## Evidence

- Real executable CLI and authenticated loopback WebSocket regression: hold `node.list` for camera list, or return its exact unknown-method error and hold `node.pair.list` for location get. Send SIGINT after the lookup arrives and observe the CLI interruption diagnostic. Both require socket closure without releasing the lookup response, exit 130, empty stdout and no `node.invoke`.
- Base `d32ac41084fcaef1099ecdbfeb1cfa81da532642`: both cases fail because the fixture must release the held response for shutdown to finish. Repair: both pass, without any node rows or camera/location access.
- Six focused files: 53 tests passed on macOS. The complete executable CLI file passed 13 tests in 27.22s; five node RPC/command siblings passed 40 tests in 4.01s. Combined wrapper: 37.26s. Final regression cases: 658ms and 931ms. Earlier cold proof includes worker compilation, not just test execution.
- Four-file formatting, docs MDX, docs inventory and diff/privacy checks passed. Scoped changed-file lint and type checks passed.
- Fresh independent implementation/test review: no findings. Author simplification/test audit keeps one shared owner and two distinct transport cases in the existing process fixture. Production +1 net line, tests +73, docs +3.
- Full local ClawSweeper review of `d32ac41084fcaef1099ecdbfeb1cfa81da532642..7ddaf8e5f192f7f1a07328cab39e626c1079f2e4`: four of four files, 191 history blobs, no fetch or truncation; patch correct, no correctness or security findings. The reviewer did not receive execution logs; actual sanitized output is below.

The POSIX signal cases are skipped on Windows. This is executable CLI proof through a protocol fixture; no live Gateway, device, model or cross-platform runtime qualification is claimed. PR CI supplies broad validation.
